headline: Stocks pared steep AI-led losses on Nov 25 (S&P 500 -0.25%, Nasdaq -0.62% after falling as much as 4.6%; Dow +0.33% to 50,182.95) as core PCE rose to 3.3% and Q3 GDP was revised up to 4.3%; US markets are closed today and close at 1pm ET Friday.
regime: Hiking regime with a volatile, rotating tape: the Fed funds target is 3.75-4.00%, a 25bp hike on Dec 9 is about 98% priced (CME FedWatch 97.8%), the 10-year is 4.85%, the VIX closed at 28.29 and the Nasdaq is down 7.3% for November.

lean.why: US markets are closed Thursday; S&P 500 futures were up about 0.3% and Asian and European stocks rose (Nikkei +0.9%, DAX +1.8%). Friday's session ends at 1pm ET, so volume is usually thin.
A Dec 9 hike is about 98% priced after core PCE hit 3.3%; the jobs report (Dec 4), FOMC (Dec 9) and CPI (Dec 10) follow, and new tariff proposals on 14 trading partners add uncertainty.
Q3 GDP grew 4.3%, but a hiking Fed, a 4.85% 10-year yield and proposed tariffs pressure valuations; the Nasdaq-100 briefly fell 20% from its record on Nov 25.

rates.n: Williams says inflation remains too high (Schwab, Nov 25); Waller said in mid-November a 50bp hike might be necessary if inflation does not improve; next FOMC Dec 8-9
CME FedWatch 97.8% for a 25bp hike on Nov 25; Polymarket 94%, Kalshi 93% (Capp Notes, Nov 25)
Freddie Mac survey released Wed Nov 25 (early for Thanksgiving), down from 7.28%; 15-year 6.54%; year ago 6.23%
$3,534.70 on Nov 25, -0.71%, after dipping below $3,500 intraday (Capp Notes)
$83.68 on Nov 25, +1.99%; Brent $94.61, +3.51% (Capp Notes); WTI $84.10 Thursday morning (AP)
28.29 on Nov 25, +7.32%, after topping 30 in the morning (Capp Notes)

sectors.why: Nvidia -3.91% and Micron -4.53% on Nov 25 (Lam Research -5.68%); S&P warned it could cut Nvidia's credit rating. AI stocks led Asia higher Thursday (Kioxia +12.6%).
Nutanix -15.19% on a CEO transition, Oracle -5.13%; tech was the worst sector (-0.83%). Salesforce and Snowflake report Dec 2.
Financials +0.71% on Nov 25; a December hike (97.8%) supports lending margins.
30-year mortgage fell to 7.21% from 7.28%; Oct new home sales rose to a 701K annual rate; Dream Finders +9.24%, real estate +0.92%.
Gold -0.71% to $3,534.70 after dipping below $3,500 intraday; elevated real yields and a firm dollar weigh.
WTI +1.99% to $83.68 and Brent +3.51% to $94.61 on Middle East tensions; energy sector +0.74%.
Discretionary -0.20%, Amazon -3.1%, Urban Outfitters -10.33%; Adobe sees Black Friday online sales of $12.9B (+9.2%) while NRF expects 182.7M weekend shoppers.
Health care -0.56% on Nov 25; Vertex -7.26% after hours after the FDA pushed its povetacicept decision to Feb 28, 2027.
Russell 2000 +0.71% to 2,704.06 and MidCap 400 +1.23% while the Nasdaq fell 0.62%.
Utilities +0.48% as the 10-year fell 6bp to 4.85%; AES leaves the S&P 500 on Dec 2.
Deere +4.44% despite an EPS miss, CNH +8.00%; industrials +0.83%, materials +2.07% (best sector).
WTI near $84 and Brent near $95 raise fuel costs; Avis Budget rose 9.62% on Nov 25.

news.head: World shares rise on Thanksgiving; US futures up 0.3%
news.mean: With US markets closed, S&P 500 futures rose 0.3% and Dow futures 0.2%. The Nikkei gained 0.9%, the Hang Seng 1.2%, the Taiex 2.5% and the Kospi 0.3% after a 6.2% drop the day before; the DAX rose 1.8% and the CAC 40 1.6% early. SoftBank rose 7.3% and Kioxia 12.6%. US crude was $84.10, up 0.4%.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: moves during a US holiday can fade or reverse once US cash trading resumes, especially in a thin half-day session.
news.today: No US trading today; Friday's session closes at 1pm ET with bonds at 2pm.
news.later: Investors may watch whether the overseas rebound in AI stocks carries into US trading.

news.head: Nasdaq dives 4.6% intraday, then pares loss to 0.6%; Dow rises
news.srcN: Reuters via Investing.com, Nov 25; Capp Notes, Nov 25
news.mean: The Dow rose 0.33% to 50,182.95, the S&P 500 fell 0.25% to 7,182.78 and the Nasdaq fell 0.62% to 23,585.80 after falling as much as 4.6%; the Nasdaq-100 briefly sat 20% below its record close. Reuters cited AI worries centered on Nvidia, new tariff proposals and rising inflation and oil. The Nasdaq is down 7.3% for November; the Russell 2000 rose 0.71%.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: a large intraday drop that is mostly recovered by the close shows dip buying, but it does not by itself mark a bottom.
news.today: Markets are closed; Friday's half-day may test whether Wednesday's recovery holds.
news.later: Investors may watch whether the Nasdaq-100 closes 20% below its record, a common bear-market definition.

news.head: October PCE inflation rises to 3.8%; core 3.3%, above forecasts
news.srcN: Trend & Ticker, Nov 25; Capp Notes, Nov 25
news.mean: Headline PCE rose 0.3% m/m and 3.8% y/y; core rose 0.3% m/m and 3.3% y/y versus a 3.2% consensus (Capp Notes). Personal income jumped 0.7% (partly one-time Medicare rebates), spending rose 0.3% with real spending flat, and the saving rate was 4.1%.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: a core PCE reading above forecast usually firms up hike bets, but yields can still fall if growth or risk worries dominate the day.
news.today: No trading today; the next inflation read is November CPI on Dec 10.
news.later: Investors may watch whether core inflation keeps rising from 3.1% in September to 3.3% and beyond.

news.head: Q3 GDP revised up to 4.3% from 3.4%
news.mean: Real GDP grew at a 4.3% annualized rate in the second estimate, up from 3.4% and above the 3.5% expected (Schwab). Final sales to private domestic purchasers rose 5.8%, and corporate profits rose $206.0B versus $384.0B in Q2.
news.hist: Q2 growth was 2.2%, so the revised Q3 figure is about twice as fast.
news.today: Strong growth plus 3.3% core inflation strengthens the case for a hike.
news.later: Schwab notes the revision adds weight to the debate over extending hikes into early 2027.

news.head: December hike odds rise to 97.8% after PCE
news.srcN: Capp Notes, Nov 25; Schwab, Nov 25; Longbridge, Nov 26
news.mean: CME FedWatch showed 97.8% odds of a 25bp hike on Dec 9 (Polymarket 94%, Kalshi 93%), which would lift the target to 4.00-4.25% from 3.75-4.00%. NY Fed President Williams said inflation remains too high (Schwab); Gov. Waller said in mid-November a 50bp hike might be necessary if inflation does not improve (Longbridge).
news.hist: Rule of thumb: when a move is about 98% priced, the reaction usually depends on guidance about the next meeting rather than the move itself.
news.today: With the hike nearly fully priced, the Dec 4 jobs report mainly moves the 50bp odds.
news.later: Investors may focus on whether the Fed signals another hike in early 2027.

news.head: Nvidia falls 3.9% as S&P warns of a possible credit downgrade
news.srcN: Stock Titan, Nov 25; AP via BNN Bloomberg, Nov 26
news.mean: Nvidia closed down 3.91% after a 31.48% jump Monday and a fall Tuesday. S&P Global Ratings put its rating on watch for a possible cut, citing management and governance concerns after Jensen Huang's reinstatement. Micron fell 4.53%, AMD 1.75%; Lam Research was down 11.64% at 11am and closed -5.68% (Capp Notes).
news.hist: Rule of thumb: credit-rating watches on mega-cap issuers rarely change funding costs much right away, but they can keep governance headlines in focus.
news.today: Asian AI stocks rebounded Thursday; Nvidia rose in late trading Wednesday (no figure given).
news.later: Investors may watch for S&P's final rating decision and the reported Dec 1 House interview with Huang.

news.head: US proposes new Section 301 tariffs on 14 trading partners
news.srcN: Global Trade & Sanctions Law, Nov 25; Stock Titan, Nov 25
news.mean: USTR proposed tariffs over structural excess capacity: up to 20% on most Chinese goods (40% fallback), 15% net of MFN for the EU, Japan, Korea and Taiwan, 18% for Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand, and up to 35% for Vietnam and 25% for India if no deal. No effective date is set; comments are due Jan 5, 2027 and hearings start Jan 25.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: proposed tariffs with long comment periods often move markets less than final tariffs, and rates can change in negotiations.
news.today: Watch for trading partners' responses over the holiday.
news.later: Investors may watch the Jan 5 comment deadline and the Jan 10 expiry of the US-China truce.

news.head: Beige Book: 8 of 12 districts grew, wages picked up
news.srcN: Federal Reserve Beige Book via Minneapolis Fed, Nov 25
news.mean: Eight districts reported slight to moderate growth and four were unchanged. Consumer spending was little changed as households stayed price sensitive. Employment rose slightly, wages rose moderately (up from modest), and prices increased moderately, with costs outpacing selling prices.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: the Beige Book rarely moves markets on its own, but rising wage pressure supports a tighter Fed.
news.today: Wage pressure adds to the hike case already set by PCE.
news.later: Investors may watch whether flat spending shows up in holiday sales.

news.head: Jobless claims fall to 189,000, tying the 2026 low
news.mean: Initial claims fell 13,000 to 189,000 for the week ended Nov 21, versus a 200,000 estimate; continuing claims fell 95,000 to 1.70 million. Seasonal factors had expected a rise of about 31,000 before Thanksgiving, which explains much of the drop.
news.hist: 189,000 ties the 2026 low first reached in the week ending July 18.
news.today: Holiday seasonal adjustments make this week's figure less reliable.
news.later: The Nov jobs report on Dec 4 gives a fuller picture.

news.head: 30-year mortgage rate dips to 7.21%; new home sales rise
news.srcN: Freddie Mac via GlobeNewswire, Nov 25; Stock Titan, Nov 25
news.mean: Freddie Mac's survey, released a day early for Thanksgiving, showed the 30-year at 7.21% (from 7.28%) and the 15-year at 6.54% (from 6.66%). October new home sales rose to a 701,000 annual rate (Stock Titan).
news.hist: A year earlier the 30-year averaged 6.23%, about one point lower.
news.today: Sam Khater said the dip offers modest relief for buyers.
news.later: A December hike could push mortgage rates back up if long yields rise.

news.head: Deere rises 4.4% despite an EPS miss and softer 2027 outlook
news.mean: Q4 revenue was $12.12B (-2%) versus about $10.4B expected; EPS of $3.89 missed the $4.03 consensus. Deere guided fiscal 2027 net income to $4.5B-5.25B (FY2026: $4.86B), including a $250M-400M pension charge, and expects about $300M in net tariff headwinds. Shares closed +4.44% (Stock Titan).
news.hist: Rule of thumb: cyclical stocks often rise on weak results when investors think the cycle is bottoming.
news.later: Investors may watch early-order trends and tariff costs.

news.head: HP jumps 11.5%; Nutanix, Urban Outfitters slide; Vertex falls late on FDA delay
news.mean: HP Inc rose 11.49% after Q4 revenue of $16.0B (+9.3%). Nutanix fell 15.19% (revenue $772.4M, +15%) as its CEO will step down. Urban Outfitters fell 10.33% despite record Q3 sales of $1.67B. Vertex fell 7.26% after hours after the FDA moved its povetacicept decision to Feb 28, 2027 from Nov 30. Anthropic closed at $82.79, just below its $83 IPO price.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: regulatory delays often hit a stock on uncertainty even when they are not rejections.
news.today: Vertex's after-hours drop will be tested in Friday's half-day.
news.later: Investors may watch the Feb 28, 2027 FDA date for Vertex.

news.head: Oil jumps 2% to $83.68, Brent +3.5%; gold dips below $3,500 intraday
news.srcN: Capp Notes, Nov 25; AP via BNN Bloomberg, Nov 26
news.mean: WTI rose 1.99% to $83.68 and Brent 3.51% to $94.61; AP notes Brent was about $72 before the war began in late February. Gold fell 0.71% to $3,534.70 after briefly dropping below $3,500, while the dollar index slipped 0.10% to 103.71.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: gold tends to struggle when real yields are high and the Fed is hiking, even during geopolitical stress.
news.today: Middle East headlines may move crude in thin holiday trading.
news.later: Higher oil feeds headline inflation ahead of the Dec 10 CPI.

news.head: Holiday outlook: Adobe sees $12.9B Black Friday online; NRF expects fewer shoppers
news.mean: Adobe forecasts US online holiday sales of $275.1B (+6.7%), Cyber Week of $47.5B (+7.4%), Black Friday $12.9B (+9.2%) and Cyber Monday $15.1B (+6.2%). NRF expects 182.7M Thanksgiving-weekend shoppers versus a 186.9M forecast last year, and forecasts Nov-Dec sales up 4.2% to $1.013T.
news.hist: In 2025, NRF forecast 186.9M Thanksgiving-weekend shoppers, and a record 202.9M actually shopped.
news.today: Early Black Friday readings arrive Friday during a half-day session.
news.later: Investors may compare Adobe's tallies with the forecasts after Cyber Monday (Nov 30).

calendar.t: Black Friday: stocks close 1pm ET, bonds 2pm; advance goods trade balance and retail/wholesale inventories (8:30am); BridgeBio FDA decision (BBP-418)
calendar.usual: Thin holiday volume; early shopping tallies drive retail headlines; binary move in BBIO.
Online sales tallies move e-commerce and retail names.

calendar.t: ISM manufacturing PMI (Nov) and JOLTS (Oct, 10am ET); Marvell and Okta earnings (after the close); House interview with Nvidia CEO reported
calendar.usual: Strong data supports the hike case; Marvell reads through to AI chips.

calendar.t: ADP employment (Nov); BMO (before the open); Salesforce, Snowflake, Five Below (after the close); SharkNinja replaces AES in the S&P 500
calendar.usual: ADP previews Friday's jobs report; Salesforce is a software sentiment check.
Usually a small mover unless far from about 200K.
A strong report raises 50bp odds; a weak one eases them.

calendar.t: Q3 productivity and costs, revised (8:30am ET); FOMC meeting begins
calendar.usual: Unit labor costs feed the inflation debate.
A 25bp hike is about 98% priced, so guidance drives the reaction.
First inflation read after the decision; a hot print raises early-2027 hike bets.

scen.title: What if November payrolls (Dec 4, 8:30am ET) are... (October was +165K with 4.1% unemployment; consensus not yet confirmed)

opts.l: Hot (payrolls well above October's +165K, unemployment at or below 4.1%)
In line (payrolls near October's pace, unemployment near 4.1%)
Cold (payrolls well below +165K or unemployment rising above 4.1%)

playbook: Homebuilders, REITs, utilities, small caps and unprofitable growth are pressured first. Banks and the dollar hold up better.
Housing, small caps, growth and gold benefit. Mortgage rates ease a few weeks later.
Gold and miners, emerging markets and big multinationals gain. Importers lose.
Energy stocks win. Airlines, cruise lines and shippers lose. Headline inflation rises, adding to hike pressure.
A growth and small-cap rally is the usual response. Banks lose some margin tailwind.
Bonds rally, defensives (healthcare, staples, utilities) lead. Cyclicals and banks get hit by recession worries.
